clue.text: Innkeepers give people a short answer

parts.note: the public is the people at large
ANS is a standard abbreviation of answer

explanation.surface: Publicans are curt with their customers, giving them brief replies.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican keeps a pub, a British tavern, so publicans are innkeepers.

clue.text: To smoke which is a sign of — bravery

definitions.text: To smoke which is a sign of — bravery

parts.words: To smoke which is a sign of — bravery
parts.note: the pause makes it read as smoking as a show of courage, but it is something smoked as a sign of peace by braves

explanation.surface: Smoking as a show of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: A brave is a Native American warrior; the pipe was smoked to seal peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A calumet smoked by Native Americans to mark a truce.

clue.text: He is swallowed by a snake for tea

indicators.note: the snake takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a boa is a snake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is swallowed whole by a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea.

clue.text: Like a youngster put in prison at the centre

indicators.note: the little word goes at the centre of the word for imprison

parts.note: to immure is to imprison
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young offender is locked up in a detention centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish and undeveloped, as the young are.

clue.text: The councillor, from Tree Island

parts.note: an alder is a tree
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A local politician hails from an island named after a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a borough council.

clue.text: Subject to surrender

explanation.surface: Placed under someone's power until giving in.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit a thing to a test is to subject it, and to submit is to yield or give in.

clue.text: Stick in the name of a sculptor

parts.note: a rod is a stick
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sculptor's name is being pinned on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is read as its own letters, not as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: Rob him maybe of diamonds

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters of the two words are one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: A thief might relieve a man of his jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi are diamond-shaped figures, rhombus being the geometric name.

clue.text: How to avoid boundless uncertainty

parts.note: boundless looks like 'limitless', but it means lacking boundaries, which marking limits avoids

explanation.surface: Advice on escaping endless doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark out limits or boundaries clearly removes doubt about where they lie.

clue.text: Railwaymen have points to take care of

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
S, south, is a compass point
E, east, is another compass point

explanation.surface: Train workers have reasons to be looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to look after them.

clue.text: Abashed by a bogus press chief

parts.note: a sham is something fake or bogus
the editor heads a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss who is a fraud is put to shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed and ashamed are synonyms for feeling embarrassment.

clue.text: A common mistake in the garden

explanation.surface: A gardener makes an everyday error.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a blunder, and also a flowering plant growing in a garden bed.

clue.text: How MPs perform, with laws

parts.note: reads like a comment on MPs' acting skills, but describes what Parliament does to bills: makes them statute

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament put on a performance with legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a bill into statute is the legislative act parliament carries out; the word also hides 'act', to perform.

clue.text: Pay me back by involving me with a bruiser

indicators.note: the letters of the second 'me' and the bruiser are tangled up together, as something involved is complicated

explanation.surface: Someone demands repayment by threatening to send round a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ME plus BRUISER, signalled by 'involving', gives the nine letters; 'with a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To refund someone what they spent is to pay them back.

clue.text: Tell nearly everyone it's without ceremony

parts.note: to inform is to tell

indicators.note: nearly means the word for everyone loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Telling the whole gathering something in a casual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something casual or relaxed is done without ceremony.

clue.text: Over-zealous wind-raiser gets an old Siamese coin

parts.note: a fan stirs up a breeze
A is the indefinite article
the tical was a former silver coin of Siam, now Thailand

explanation.surface: A keen windbag pockets some old Thai money.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanatical means excessively zealous.

clue.text: Just a loud tune

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Nothing but a noisy melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and just both mean even-handed and impartial.

clue.text: Home distribution of nicer seed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are dealt out into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden centre's sale of better seeds to households.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling or home.

clue.text: Moan like Gray's moping owl

explanation.surface: Grumbling like the bird in a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, the moping owl does to the moon complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan is to grumble, and the owl in Gray's Elegy does to the moon grumble.

clue.text: Photographing old Bob asleep

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S
napping means dozing, asleep

explanation.surface: Taking pictures of an aged man called Bob while he dozes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is slang for a shilling, the pre-decimal coin written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking snaps, quick photographs.

clue.text: By the sound of it, deserve the bird

indicators.note: signals that the word for deserve is heard and spelt another way

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Someone appears to merit being jeered off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bird' looks like a jeer (getting the bird) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle.

clue.text: Sign-posts at Cruft's ?

explanation.surface: Direction signs set up at a famous dog show.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicators that show the way, and gun dogs of a breed seen at Crufts, Britain's leading dog show.

clue.text: Merrymaking by French central police

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word police are taken

explanation.surface: French police at the centre of festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes OLIC, the middle of 'police'; 'by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is light-hearted fun or merrymaking.

clue.text: Sensation caused by' "The Endless Stream "

indicators.note: the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A novel titled The Endless Stream causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase looks like a title; 'Endless' trims THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden sensation of excitement.

clue.text: Job for a fellow taking coach to the vessel

parts.note: a coach is a private tutor
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A man is taking a bus down to the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus; here it means a teacher. 'taking' and 'to the' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A university fellow often holds the post of tutor, so the position is his job.

clue.text: The father to whom Macaulay's Romans prayed

definitions.text: The father to whom Macaulay's Romans prayed

parts.words: The father to whom Macaulay's Romans prayed
parts.note: points to Horatius in Lays of Ancient Rome, where the hero prays to the river as a father

explanation.surface: A deity worshipped by Romans in a Victorian poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay's Horatius cries 'Oh Tiber! father Tiber! To whom the Romans pray'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's river, addressed as a father god in Macaulay's ballad.

clue.text: Is "Smoke gets in your eyes " relayed thus ?

definitions.text: Is "Smoke gets in your eyes " relayed thus ?

parts.words: Is "Smoke gets in your eyes " relayed thus ?
parts.note: the song title is played over loudspeakers as background music, and smoke suggests a tobacco pipe

explanation.surface: Asks how a popular song is broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoke Gets in Your Eyes is a 1930s popular song; background music relayed through speakers is called piped, which also suits smoke from a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Music transmitted through a building's speakers is described as piped.

clue.text: Animal found in the Himalayas and in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: the word and goes inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature living both in the Himalayas and in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to list two habitats; 'and' is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda lives in the Himalayan forests.

clue.text: With a hundred break in billiards opening, they make one sick

indicators.note: the two pieces break into the opening letters of the next word
the start of the word billiards is taken

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A century break at the start of a billiards game, though the bugs bring illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' suggests a billiards break of a hundred; here A and C break into BILLI, the opening of 'billiards'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, some of which cause disease.

clue.text: Scene of dancing at a bridge party

definitions.text: Scene of dancing at a bridge party

parts.words: Scene of dancing at a bridge party
parts.note: a bridge party sounds like card players, but the French song has people dancing on a bridge in this city

explanation.surface: Where people dance at a card-playing evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The French nursery song Sur le pont d'Avignon has everyone dancing on the bridge there.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city's famous bridge is where the song says people dance.

clue.text: Memento of high priest found in church

indicators.note: the priest is placed within the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic, a church
Eli was the high priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A keepsake of a senior cleric discovered in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a memento of the past or of a saint.

clue.text: Potentate denied burial at sea ?

explanation.surface: A ruler refused a burial at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone denied burial at sea would have a grave on land.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a German count ruling a territory; read as land grave, a burial place on dry ground.
